newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek yield curve frozen in late dull dealings.
newsitem.headline: Greek yield curve frozen in late dull dealings.

text.p: Greek depos and implied drachma rates from forex forwards were gyrating around morning levels in thin, unexciting late trade after the treasury announced lower coupon and base rates on bonds to be auctioned December 27, dealers said.
"There is very little movement and very little interest for trading before Christmas and therefore depos and implied drachma rates are almost unchnaged since this morning," the dealer said.
Forex and bond markets were also quiet with trading activity subdued, dealers said.
The finance ministry announced that its three-year, 100 billion drachma bond to be auctioned on December 27 will feature a lower coupon at 10.70 percent from 11 percent previously.
The seven-year, 200 billion drachma FRN to be auctioned the same day will also feature a lower base rate of 11.20 percent, down from 11.50 percent at the previous auction.
The central bank kept its overnight bid unchanged at 12.40 percent and dealers said they were bracing for a much awaited cut, perhaps sizeable, in the next few weeks.
The mark was quoted at 159.00/10 drachmas from Monday's 159.000 fix, the dollar at 247.10/20 drachmas from 246.580 and the Ecu at 306.34/46 from 306.220 drachmas.
